raw_response:
I farm 18 mu, and I have to keep the whole year steady, not just chase one crop. I have 10 years of experience, my family has 4 people, and I have well irrigation, so I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize system because that is the safest way for me to hold grain output and cash flow. I will not spread myself too thin with vegetables, because cabbage and eggplant need more watching, more spraying, and more labor at the right time. I will keep those on smaller areas for income, and I will keep stevia as a cash crop on a moderate area because it can bring money but I do not want to risk too much land on it. For wheat and maize, I will use improved or hybrid seed and put in enough fertilizer to keep yields stable. For vegetables, I will use more fertilizer and more pesticide than grain crops because they need cleaner leaves and better growth. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate enough to avoid drought stress, but I will still control costs and not overwater. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale and fits how I manage land. I am choosing this mix because it balances food, cash income, labor, and risk across the year.
